party_summary: Arcanine + Snorlax leading; Magearna* / Whimsicott / Weavile / Iron Leaves* reserve. Magearna entered. Party was deliberately built to be indifferent to Trick Room rather than to race it.

driver.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark, native AI. Not earned campaign play.

attempts.narrative: T1 Flare Blitz (2x on Steel) removed Honedge and Porygon set Trick Room at the end of the turn. T2 the room converted immediately: Gimmighoul's Power Gem (2x on Fire) and Porygon's Tri Attack both resolved before Arcanine's Flare Blitz and killed it. T3 Magearna replaced Arcanine and Porygon Protected away a lethal Flash Cannon. T4 the AI pivoted a damaged Porygon out and fed Wooloo to the Flash Cannon; Gimmighoul Protected a lethal Crunch. T5 Flash Cannon removed Wooloo, Gimmighoul pivoted out and the room expired. T6 Flash Cannon removed Porygon as it tried to re-set the room. T7 Flash Cannon finished Gimmighoul.

ai_positive_notes: The T2 room payoff is the clearest demonstration of the TRICK_ROOM flag in the block: two zero-Speed-IV bodies moved before a base 95 Speed attacker and removed it before its queued move.

Two separate preservation pivots - Porygon out to Wooloo on T4, Gimmighoul out to Porygon on T5 - each fed a fresher body to my attack and kept a damaged member alive. Combined with E0010 and E0011, switch evaluation is consistently the strongest part of this AI's play in this block.
T6 re-selecting Trick Room the turn after it expired, rather than earlier while it was still up, is exactly the 'do not endlessly retry the setter' discipline the plan asks for.

level_changes.rule_applied: Won on the first attempt with 1 player faint. The room did convert into a KO, but Magearna and Snorlax were never in danger after that, so this is the +1 case rather than the keep case.

unchanged.reason: already the joint-highest member and it personally blocked two kills

level_changes.reasoning: Porygon carries the room and is the lowest member together with Honedge; one level makes the setter likelier to survive the double-target the counterplay list recommends against it. Honedge is raised for the same reason - it is the member the room is built to enable, and at L14 with 49 HP it dies to a single super-effective hit before the room it is waiting for even exists, which is why Swords Dance and No Guard are both still unverified.

could_this_be_cooler.answer: Yes. There is one concrete mismatch worth fixing and one ordering problem.
could_this_be_cooler.keep: A full zero-Speed-IV Trick Room team at cap 14, with the room actually converting into a KO on the turn after it goes up, is a real and well-built lesson, and it is the only team in this block that changes the rules of the fight rather than just trading damage. The disposition line about choosing Speed IVs by matchup instead of inferring zero from Quiet/Brave is clearly being honoured.
could_this_be_cooler.suggestion: Porygon's DOWNLOAD raised Attack on both entries, and Porygon is QUIET with Tri Attack and Thunderbolt - two special moves and no physical move at all. Against any player team whose Defence total is lower than its Special Defence total, this ability is dead weight on the team's most important member. Either give Porygon a physical option worth the boost (Return, Facade) or switch the set to something that wants the ability it has. Analytic would also fit a Trick Room setter far better, since it rewards moving last outside the room.
could_this_be_cooler.second_thought: Wooloo's Fluffy is the team's punish for a Fire lead, and Wooloo is the LAST member to arrive. In this fight Arcanine was dead two turns before Wooloo appeared, so the interaction that the team is built to threaten never met the threat. Leading Wooloo beside Porygon - the plan already names 'Porygon and Wooloo form a bulkier room mode' as the alternate deployment - would put the Fluffy body in front of the Fire attacker while the room goes up, which is a much better fight.
